title: Mid-game supply in 4-player games: measure first, then propose one fix
problem: Informal feedback (REP-045): "supply cant keep up with demand" from mid-game and players ended up with nothing to buy. By code: no lorry comes on Market Days (days 3, 6, 9, 12; game.ts), and 4 shops add 1 of each fruit (about 17 fruits on a lorry day against a buying capacity of 16 for four shops). This is a hypothesis; no one has measured it.
scope: Step 1, no game change: simulate 2, 3 and 4 shop games and measure, per day, how much of each fruit is on the market before each shop buys, how often a shop finds the fruit it wants gone, and how this differs on Market Days
Step 2: propose one change with options and same-seed before and after results (candidates: a smaller delivery on Market Days, or more supply for 4 shops); the owner picks
Step 3, after the owner picks: implement, bump RULES_VERSION, update RULES.md and data, run the checks
Any change must be playable by hand with cards (DEC-027)
exclusions: Changing customers, prices, specialities or computer players

acceptance.text: Measurement report shows supply against demand per day for 2, 3 and 4 shops, with sample size
Owner sets a target (for example, the largest share of shop turns that may find nothing to buy) before any change is chosen
After the change: same-seed comparison meets the owner target; verify and verify:full pass
A human playtest of the changed rules (not computer only) is recorded or explicitly deferred by the owner
